reported_failure.error: Actual desktop Slurm job partition differs from the profile

defect: The scontrol field parser recognized word-only keys. Slurm's AllocNode:Sid key following Partition caused Partition=local to parse as 'local AllocNode:Sid=system:8749'. The workflow also independently used the same deficient parsing pattern.
fix: Recognize colon-separated scontrol field keys while preserving values containing spaces and rejecting duplicate fields.
Use the already verified job record for workflow identity checks instead of a second scheduler query and parser.
Include expected and observed partition values in genuine mismatch errors.

regressions.before_fix: Both CPU and CUDA allocation-format regressions failed with the reported partition error.
regressions.after_fix: Both pass; raw job/step workflow integrations also pass for accuracy and neural stages. Existing ownership, partition, account, root, node/task and GPU allocation mismatch checks remain active.

test_run.command: OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 MKL_NUM_THREADS=1 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/test_desktop_slurm_runtime.py tests/test_fedora_workflow.py tests/test_fedora_setup.py tests/test_premix_workflow.py tests/test_desktop_runtime.py tests/test_carc_integration.py --basetemp=.runtime/pytest-fedora-partition-fix --junitxml=.runtime/fedora-partition-fix.xml

scope: Cloud CPU tests with mocked Slurm records. No actual Fedora submission or CUDA computation occurred. Native verification requires a fresh allocated smoke on the desktop.
recovery: Pull main and run bash scripts/fedora_slurm.sh run --smoke. Preserve the failed run; existing Python venv and local partition profile can be reused.
